paragraphs.paragraph: Hosea, the Prophet and Living Symbol
paragraphs.title: Hosea, the Prophet and Living Symbol

easy.explanation: The first verse calls Hosea the son of Beeri.

answers: The kings of Judah and Jeroboam, king of Israel
easy.explanation: The passage names the kings of Judah and Jeroboam, king of Israel.
easy.q: During the days of which kings did the word of the LORD come to Hosea?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms.”
easy.q: What did the LORD tell Hosea to take?

medium.explanation: Hosea went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim.
medium.q: What did Hosea do after receiving the LORD's command?

medium.explanation: The verse says that Gomer conceived and bare Hosea a son.
medium.q: What was born after Gomer conceived?

medium.explanation: The phrase appears in the LORD's command concerning a wife and children of whoredoms.
medium.q: In the passage, what does the phrase “children of whoredoms” refer to?

answers: A symbolic picture of the relationship between Israel and God
The founding of a new kingdom
challenge.explanation: Hosea's marriage and family serve as a living symbol of Israel's relationship with the LORD.
challenge.q: What does Hosea's mission represent in the passage?

answers: To identify the period in which Hosea prophesied
To list the names of Hosea's children
challenge.explanation: The list of kings establishes the historical period of Hosea's prophetic ministry.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention both the kings of Judah and the king of Israel?

answers: His household becomes a visible sign of Israel's condition before God
His life describes the building of the temple
His life explains the order of Judah's kings
challenge.explanation: Hosea's marriage and children portray the relationship between Israel and the LORD.
challenge.q: How are Hosea's personal experiences connected to his prophetic message?

paragraphs.idea: Hosea, the Prophet and Living Symbol

paragraphs.paragraph: Jezreel and Judgment on the Kingdom of Israel
paragraphs.title: Jezreel and Judgment on the Kingdom of Israel

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded, “Call his name Jezreel.”
easy.q: What name was the LORD's servant commanded to give the first son?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.”
easy.q: What did the LORD say He would do to the kingdom of Israel?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “And she conceived again, and bare a daughter.”

answers: I will require an account for the bloodshed
medium.explanation: The statement announces judgment for the bloodshed associated with Jezreel.
medium.q: What does “I will avenge the blood of Jezreel” mean in context?

answers: It announces judgment for the blood of Jezreel upon Jehu's house
It identifies where Jehu's house lived
It is another name for the house of Jehu
medium.explanation: The verse connects Jezreel with avenging its blood upon the house of Jehu.
medium.q: How is the name Jezreel connected with the house of Jehu?

answers: The withdrawal of mercy from Israel
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel.”

answers: The avenging of blood is connected with the ending of Israel's kingdom
The avenging of blood concerns only the birth of a daughter
The avenging of blood cancels the judgment
challenge.explanation: The passage links judgment for Jezreel with causing the kingdom of Israel to cease.
challenge.q: How are the two judgments concerning Jezreel connected?

answers: The meaning of the daughter's name
challenge.explanation: A broken bow symbolizes the defeat and removal of Israel's military strength.
challenge.q: What does breaking Israel's bow in the valley of Jezreel emphasize?

answers: Judgment at Jezreel, withdrawal of mercy, and eventual removal
challenge.explanation: Jezreel announces judgment, Lo-ruhamah announces withdrawn mercy, and the passage continues with the taking away of Israel.
challenge.q: What sequence of messages is represented by the names in this section?

paragraphs.idea: Jezreel and Judgment on the Kingdom of Israel

paragraphs.paragraph: The Distinction Between Judah and Israel and the Final Rupture
paragraphs.title: The Distinction Between Judah and Israel and the Final Rupture

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will have mercy upon the house of Judah.”
easy.q: Upon whom does the LORD say He will have mercy?

easy.explanation: The verse says Judah will be saved “by the LORD their God.”
easy.q: By whom will the LORD save the house of Judah?
What name was given to the third son?

answers: It would not be accomplished by bow, sword, battle, horses, or horsemen
It would be accomplished only by horsemen
It would require a great army
medium.explanation: The verse specifically says the LORD would not save Judah by those instruments of war.
medium.q: How would Judah's salvation differ from the military methods listed in the verse?

answers: Because Israel was no longer God's people
Because Israel had won a battle
Because Judah received a new name
medium.explanation: The name is explained by the words, “Ye are not my people.”

answers: The LORD will show compassion to Judah
medium.explanation: To have mercy means to show compassion and favor.
medium.q: What does “I will have mercy” mean in the sentence about the house of Judah?

answers: Judah receives mercy and salvation, while Israel is denied mercy
Judah is punished while Israel is saved
Both are saved in exactly the same way
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes Judah's mercy and salvation from Israel's judgment.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast between Judah and Israel in this passage?

answers: It expresses a broken relationship between Israel and God
It identifies the place where the son was born
challenge.explanation: The explanation of the name says, “Ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.”
challenge.q: How does the name “Lo-ammi” express more than a personal name?

answers: A symbolic prophetic mission, judgment on Israel, and a distinction between Israel and Judah
A war, the building of a city, and the crowning of a king
Mercy on Israel, judgment on Judah, and military victory
challenge.explanation: The chapter moves from Hosea's symbolic mission to judgment on Israel and then to the contrast between Judah and Israel.
challenge.q: What broad sequence of ideas appears across the three sections of the chapter?

paragraphs.idea: The Distinction Between Judah and Israel and the Final Rupture
